chunks: From him, from Ibn Ribāṭ, from Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: Jabrāʾīl عليه السلام descended upon the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.

And he narrated the hadith like the first one, and mentioned, instead of one qāmah and two qāmahs, two feet and four feet. So it is not for anyone to say that these reports indicate that the beginning and the end of the time are equal, because he said, “What is between them is a time,” since it is not impossible that what lies between the two times be made a time, even though the first is more excellent than it. And that which indicates this is:

key_terms.أَفْضَلَ: more excellent or superior in merit
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلُ: Jibrīl, the angel who brought revelation and instruction
key_terms.رَسُولِ ٱللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.قَدَمَيْنِ: two feet, an alternative measure mentioned for the timing
key_terms.ٱلْحَدِيثَ: the hadith or narrated report being referred to
key_terms.ٱلْقَامَةِ: a measure used in describing prayer time

ai.seo_question: Do Shia hadiths about the time of ẓuhr and ʿaṣr mean that the beginning and end of the prayer time are equal?
ai.summary: This report concerns the beginning time of ẓuhr and ʿaṣr and clarifies differing expressions used in related narrations, such as qāmah versus feet. It argues that the existence of a shared valid prayer time between two limits does not mean all parts of that time are equal in merit, since the earliest part may still be more excellent.
